target_customer: Product, design and research teams at software companies that run customer interviews, surveys and prototype tests
problem: Recruiting participants, scheduling interviews and sharing findings is manual and slow, and existing panel providers were expensive.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, freemium at launch with paid plans at 49 and 199 dollars per month

founders.name: Ned Dwyer
previous_startups: Elto, web developer marketplace, sold to GoDaddy in 2015
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch July 2021 and YC page. At GoDaddy he worked with the UX research team.

founders.name: PJ Murray
previous_startups: Elto, web developer marketplace, sold to GoDaddy in 2015
founders.background_notes: YC page: about 10 years of software development, mostly Rails at early-stage startups.

competitors.name: User Interviews
competitors.what: Participant recruitment and research CRM for qualitative user research

technical_complexity.rationale: Rails-style SaaS covering recruiting, scheduling, surveys and integrations. Standard engineering with some integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Customer panels and research repositories create some lock-in, but features are replicable and funded rivals existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition of Great Question found. Rivals consolidated among themselves: a January 2026 podcast page refers to UserTesting acquiring User Interviews.

market_need_then: TechCrunch quotes the founders on a large research provider costing about 40,000 dollars a year. MainStreet booked eight interviews within 24 hours of signing up.

branding.domain_note: Used greatquestion.co, later moved to greatquestion.com (the .co redirects to the .com).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and helpful. Newer headline: UX research that is as easy as asking a question

branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt June 23, 2021 per the YC page. No merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly phrase name tied to the product job and cleanly spelled, but generic in search. No sourced evidence of fan community.

outcome_analysis: Great Question is active and grew to about 41 people. After a 2.5M dollar seed in July 2021, a repeat founder team that had sold Elto to GoDaddy stayed capital efficient and reported a total of 16.6M dollars raised after a 13M Series A led by Inovia in November 2025. Customers include ServiceNow, Brex and Asana. The long gap between rounds shows slow, efficient growth in a crowded category.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch and the YC page. Series A confirmed by the company blog, also reported by SmartCompany and CB Insights listings. Company states total raised 16.6M, so coverage is complete; aggregators list 13M, 15.6M and 22.6M. The User Interviews source was seen in a search result and its date and amount come from that listing. The seed-round TechCrunch article names no competitors. Education of founders not found. An outcome search found no layoffs, acquisition or rebrand.
